title: Universal cochain counit transported from homotopy localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with chosen unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $p_{\mathcal A}:C(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal A)$ for quotient by chain homotopy, $Q^h_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for homotopy localization, and $Q_{\mathcal A}:C(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for complex localization, and likewise for $\mathcal B$. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive, with termwise functors $F^c,F^h$. Suppose $L:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $\epsilon:LQ^h_{\mathcal A}\to Q^h_{\mathcal B}F^h$ exhibit a right Kan extension: for every $G:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $a:GQ^h_{\mathcal A}\to Q^h_{\mathcal B}F^h$ there is a unique $b:G\to L$ with $\epsilon(bQ^h_{\mathcal A})=a$.
Let $\beta:LQ_{\mathcal A}\to Q_{\mathcal B}F^c$ be the canonical cochain comparison [def-derived-cochain-counit], formed by whiskering $\epsilon$ by $p_{\mathcal A}$ and conjugating by the canonical localization factorization isomorphisms [def-derived-cochain-comparison-factors]. Then $(L,\beta)$ is a right Kan extension of $Q_{\mathcal B}F^c$ along $Q_{\mathcal A}$. Explicitly, for every natural $a:GQ_{\mathcal A}\to Q_{\mathcal B}F^c$ there is a unique $b:G\to L$ with $\beta(bQ_{\mathcal A})=a$. For every complex $P$, $\beta_P$ is invertible if and only if $\epsilon_{p_{\mathcal A}P}$ is invertible. Thus the same functor, with the specified cochain counit, retains both universality and every resolving-class computation; no exactness of $F$ is assumed.

These are exactly the specified comparison maps; no replacement counit is chosen.

In the chosen localization and homotopy quotient implementations, every comparison component outside epsilon is an identity. The formula reduces to L.map (𝟙 _) ≫ epsilon.app (p.obj P) ≫ Qh.map (𝟙 _) ≫ 𝟙 _. Functor.map_id and the category identity laws therefore give beta.app P = epsilon.app (p.obj P).
